Enlightenme wrote: Hi

I understand that price bounces on FLs that are usually in key levels and therefore, they are special. However, for left shoulders in relation to QM, is it safe to assume

1. that the FLs broken to create the left shoulders (not the FL created after breaking the left shoulder) are insignificant and also are not in a key level? 2. and that the time frame to which the FLs broken to create the left shoulders belongs to is irrelevant?

I am asking this as I found what I believe to be is a QM and I was tracing the possible FL broken to create the left shoulder. And just to be sure of the FL, I look further to the left to the possible SR it broke and the possible FL the SR reacted to. When I went to the LTF, it seems that the FL the SR reacted to is an FL, not in the form of a hiccup or the letter N, but of a single candle. I had no problem with this until I can't find the FL that was broken to create the LS and therefore, am now doubtful of the LS.

Below are pictures for better understanding.

Hi,

I think sometimes it helps to actually "replay" the history you are looking at and mark things in the making. Otherwise you might end up curvefitting FLs ( meaning trying to mark FLs so that all the highs are within, whereas engulfs sometimes happen ). Look at my markings on top of your chart. I'm not saying this is correct, but look at it again with this in mind, it might help!

Cheers

I watched the video again and I realized I may have left out a line. I added a yellow line to the my drawing.

(41:00-42:30) Statement 1: (For the one encircled in violet in my drawing) IF said "This over here. Didn't make any PA as far as I can see. It didn't break the low of this (referring to all time low available at that time in the chart) and didn't really do anything back over there so its not terribly important. But what it can do is add confluence with....

Statement 2: As for the lower one(encircled in green in my drawing), IF said "This one here did actually break that low. We'll have to look at fxtop if it actually did break a significant low. It might not be a flag limit in itself..... But if this the only information that we've got, then what we're gonna go is mark the damn thing."

Statement 3: (Somewhere in the first half of the video) IF said he only cares about flags limits being created and destroyed.

Again- the question was why wasn't the low marked (encircled in violet)? My guess: we only mark the high and low of that which broke the all time high and low?

Statement 2 partially supports that. IF seems to have implied that it was marked because it broke the low. Of course we have to check whether it was a significant low with fxtop, but with the information provided it is a significant low. However, he goes on to to say that it might not be a flag limit in itself so now I think we must only mark those that break the flag limit.

On the other hand statement 3 seems to support the latter implication of statement 2.

Alright. So with statement 2 and statement 3. I have to come to conclusion that we only mark those that are flag limits (new highs or lows) from breaking all time highs and lows or other flag limits. Then again, wasn't the encircled in violet one?

Please point out where I may have been wrong.

Hi everyone,

I've been watching video course #2 and have a basic question regarding the kinks.

What I understand until now is that everything is based on FLs, which are the kinks. So in essence we could substitute the word "kink" in the place of "FL". Engulfing of a kink, creates a new kink, which in turn when engulfed, creates an even newer kink. That much I understand.

In the video (I might misinterpret what IF is teaching), it seem to me that the drawn kink on the rightmost side bypassed every other kinks on the left (hence, pointing the concept of scenario 2 in my drawing above).

What I understand until now is scenario 1, which is "the engulf of an FL creates an FL,...", i.e. we shift the boxes (FLs/Kinks) to adjust for the engulfs and retraces.

My question then is, which is the more accurate representation of the LS kink? scenario 1 or 2?

If a direct answer isn't in our best interest, then I would appreciate any form of guidance regarding this subject. Thank you all for you comments and guidance
readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/tra...or-pa?start=50#64050

HCDE

That's a well put question Frosty. My mind isn't clear about it yet. But my best guess is that kind of of both your scenarios are right in some ways. I would say that Z is a kink (RS kink of W), Y is a kink too (RS kink of the last low it broke).

But the problem with that is if you use that principles, almost everything on the chart is a kink.

Frosty

Hi HCDE,

I have been wondering about your "almost everything on the chart is a kink" statement. In essence, yes that is what I'm currently struggling to understand.

My noob educated guess: it is a matter of scale. Since in the video, IF particular LS (near the beginning of USD/CAD analysis)

I've also read a question from EM to Edge about completed FLs. I went along the lines of "A 15 minute FL needs to touch the next 15 minute FL for it to be considered completed" (close to exact words, i believe).

Bro Staurum also mentioned about managing expectations on the lower scale targets a few posts back.

What I concluded, then, is that we should pick any HTF chart, mark the barriers, find the FLs/kinks in that scale, drop to LTF to find clean orders within the kinks, watch price come back to the kinks, wait for PA on that LTF, enter trade on retrace, set target on first target IN THAT LTF.

So, I think to answer which are the right kinks for LSs, then we should first ask which TF the kinks belong to in the first place.

Am I getting closer to the truth or did I just confuse myself there?

HCDE

I just recently back to RTM, hope someone can help clear my confusion. Regarding part 2 video, IF mention places to mark to wait for PA. (LS, PCP, RS, Break into CP) and latter IF show a marked up USDCAD monthly chart with Highs & Lows line drawn.

Question: So for starter, we basically just mark the highs & lows from monthly down to LTF?and look the latest LS kink/ RS kink for further PA?

Any guidance would be much appreciate. TQ

Alfred

Yes, you can do exactly what you have just described. However, trading is not only about picking the best entries. You need to be realistic with your target. Most of the time you will get a bounce, but do not expect every monthly kink to give 1000 pips bounce every time. Identify your conservative target, take partial profit, and let the remaining position run.

I think the confusion comes from trying to maintain the zones at that particular time frame. For example, If we have our zones and PAZs on H1 then there might be hidden LTF zones in M30 or lower which are not visible on H1 that bounced price but we think it was PA. But those LTF zones might be less significant to hold price so I then avoid them.

I assume it's a factor of looking for the PA opportunities with tight SL on RT and higher RR than 1:1.
